pages.text: "Ouch!" Nia limped in the acacia shade, one front foot raised. A thorn was stuck between their hooves. "I want to go to the water, but my foot hurts."
Mom examined it. "A thorn, Nia. We need to take it out." "No! That'll hurt more!" Nia's tail pressed to their back legs. Kiki watched from a rock.
Nia lifted their foot a little. The thorn looked huge and sharp. Their heart thumped and their foot shook. "It's biting my foot and won't let go..."
Mom stood beside Nia. "It's not just a thorn. It's a thorn monster." "A monster?" Nia tilted their neck toward her. "But it fears one thing."
Mom whispered, "The word 'Pop!' Breathe out, say 'Pop!' and it'll jump out in surprise." Kiki hopped down and raised a paw. "I'll help say it!" Nia swallowed.
"I'll gently catch the thorn's tip with my mouth," Mom said. "Then we all shout, 'Pop out, thorn!'" Nia repeated softly. "I'll try." They held out their sore foot.
Nia took a big breath and squeezed their eyes shut. Mom caught the thorn's tip. "Pop out, thorn!" Kiki and Nia shouted. "Oh? It didn't hurt at all!"
On the grass, the thorn was tiny. Not a monster after all! Nia swayed their neck. "I didn't cry!" Kiki clapped.

Nia dipped their foot into the waterhole. "Washing helps it heal," Mom said. Nia knew the steps. "One, a big breath! Two, hold my foot out to Mom! Three, all together—pop out, thorn!" Cool water soothed their foot.
Mom nuzzled Nia's neck. "You were so brave." Once the thorn was out, Nia's foot could feel better. Pop out, thorn! Nia strode along the shore.
